Levels of urbanisation increased rapidly between 1950 and about 1980 [1], from just over
50 per cent to about 70 per cent [1]. They then increased more slowly to about 75 per
cent by 2025 and are predicted to rise to about 80 per cent by 2050 [1].     [Max 3 marks]

Air quality in Delhi varies between borderline satisfactory and very poor [1]. Air quality is
borderline satisfactory during the monsoon rainy season [1] as the rain takes the pollutants
out of the atmosphere [1]. Air quality is very poor between October and January [1] as this is
when there are fireworks related to Diwali festivals [1]. Stubble burning of wheat occurs in
April and May and contributes to the poor air quality [1]. Emissions from motor vehicles,
building sites, power plants and solid waste disposal contribute to poor air quality throughout
the year [1].
[Max 5 marks]

The rural-to-urban fringe is the area on the edge of a city/large urban area, where the
town meets the countryside.
[1 mark]

The advantages of the rural-to-urban fringe include much land that has not been
developed [1]; cheaper cost of land compared with inner areas [1]; good transport,
especially for motor vehicles [1]; land that has not been made derelict (brownfield sites)
[1].
[Max 3 marks]

Developments on the rural-to-urban fringe may lead to more traffic and congestion
there [1], deteriorating air quality [1]; removal of natural habitat [1] and reduced
biodiversity [1]; an increase in impermeable surface, which can lead to local
flooding [1].
[Max 4 marks]

Opportunities of urban living include a greater range of employment opportunities, varied
range of housing, improved access to services, e.g. schools, retailing and health care.
However, some urban areas are overcrowded, there can be poor environmental quality;
demand for employment may outstrip availability of resources. Answers should include
both challenges and opportunities. No more than 5 marks should be awarded in the
following instances: if the answer covers only challenges or opportunities; if the answer does
not include named examples of urban areas which provide opportunities and
challenges.
[Max 7 marks]
